source.title: Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models: A Nonlinear Perspective
source.authors: Fabian Hildebrandt; Andreas K. Maier; Patrick Krauss; Achim Schilling

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own activation-separability results and argues that refusal is nonlinear and multidimensional, refining or challenging a single-linear-direction account. It does not causally remove or add a refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The study computes harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions, but does not ablate or add them, test harmful-request compliance after intervention, measure induced refusal of harmless requests, or evaluate general capability. It reports activation geometry and GDV separability, not behavioral refusal rates. Table II reports the best (lowest) GDV for each model and dimensionality-reduction method at its listed layer; these are the study's reported separability outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study argues against a single linear refusal direction (V4-like), but its evidence does not bear on any version. It measures how well harmful and harmless prompt activations cluster in 2-D PCA, t-SNE and UMAP embeddings, scored by GDV. It never ablates or adds a direction and never measures refusal or compliance. Separation of harmful from harmless inputs is a harmfulness-class geometry, not the refusal mechanism. Lower GDV under t-SNE/UMAP than under 2-D PCA also does not show that refusal is nonlinear or multi-directional: nonlinear embeddings sharpen clusters by design, and 2-D PCA keeps maximum variance, not the class-separating direction. This is a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that harmful/harmless separation (which they call refusal) appears in all six models with architecture-specific layer patterns, and that refusal is nonlinear and multidimensional rather than a single linear direction. The paraphrase should note that this conclusion rests on embedding separability, not on any intervention or measured refusal behavior.
record.recipe_differences: They use harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means activations, following the cited approach, but analyze activation separability with PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, and GDV rather than testing causal removal or addition. This is not an intervention study.
record.method_sensitivity: Separability varies by dimensionality-reduction method and layer; the reported best layers differ across models and methods. The authors also describe architecture-specific layer patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Across six small instruct models (Llama-3.2, Qwen2, Bloom), harmful and harmless prompt activations separate better in 2-D t-SNE/UMAP embeddings (GDV -0.60 to -0.89) than in 2-D PCA (-0.40 to -0.51). Best layers differ by model family, and the text describes sub-clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful/harmless input activations are separable across layers and model families, with family-specific layer profiles; nonlinear embeddings show tighter clusters than 2-D PCA.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: The evidence is activation geometry and dimensionality-reduction separability, not causal mediation or behavioral refusal/compliance outcomes. The reported table selects best-layer GDVs; no uncertainty estimates or controls are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Layer-by-layer values and cluster patterns shown in Figures 1–4 are not separately extracted; Table II supplies the reported best-layer GDV for each model and method, while the prose gives qualitative architecture-level summaries without a distinct numeric result for every plotted layer.

untested.parts: No ablation, no addition, no refusal rates, no capability checks.
No causal test of affine, cone or multi-direction structure. The activation-geometry argument does not measure refusal.
Harmfulness clustering is measured but not compared against refusal decisions.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 'supports' label is dropped: no row measures refusal, and the PCA vs t-SNE/UMAP GDV comparison cannot establish nonlinearity. The Bloom 'misclassifying harmless instructions' remark is an activation observation, not a behavioral refusal rate. No uncertainty is reported, and Table II reports best-layer values only.

versions.untested_parts: No causal ablation or addition, refusal/compliance behavior after intervention, or general-capability test.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
No test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.

Tests nonlinear and multidimensional activation structure using dimensionality reduction and separability. Does not test affine or cone descriptions, or compare a dominant direction plus residual directions through causal interventions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Tests several model families, but not transfer of a direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary refusal-training methods or timing.

rows.note: Reported best-layer value; this linear-method result alone does not establish whether refusal is better described by multiple or nonlinear directions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Nonlinear dimensionality-reduction results across the six tested instruct models
reader_labels.reason: The reported t-SNE and UMAP GDVs are lower than the corresponding PCA values for each model, and the authors conclude that refusal representations are nonlinear and multidimensional (r2-r3, r5-r6, r8-r9, r11-r12, r14-r15, r17-r18).
